seo_title: Cost of Living in Tbilisi 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Tbilisi per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The most popular city for relocation from Russia: a liberal visa policy, affordable prices, a thriving Russian-speaking community and an active IT scene. Ideal for living car-free and getting started quickly.
pros: Visa-free entry for 365 days for Russian citizens
Very affordable housing and food prices
A large and active Russian-speaking community
A developed IT scene with plenty of coworkings and meetups
Sulphur baths and wine regions just an hour away
cons: Chaotic traffic and little parking in the centre
Hot, dry summers; heating isn't available everywhere
Rising rents driven by the influx of relocators

best_places.name: Sololaki district
best_places.description: Old balconies, wine cellars and atmospheric cafés just minutes from Freedom Square.

best_places.name: Vino Underground
best_places.description: Craft Georgian wines, cheeses and qvevri experiments in a basement bar.

best_places.name: Dry Bridge
best_places.description: A weekend antiques market — Soviet porcelain, icons, paintings and vintage finds.

best_places.name: Fabrika
best_places.description: A former sewing factory, now the city's main coworking and hangout for remote workers.

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 365 days without a visa — all you need is a passport; the stamp is issued at the border.

visa_steps.title: Personal Number
visa_steps.description: Get an ID at the House of Justice — it takes a few days and is needed for renting and opening a bank account.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Bank of Georgia or TBC Bank — both open accounts for Russians with a passport and ID.

visa_steps.title: Registered rental
visa_steps.description: The lease is recorded in the state registry — this is required for subsequent procedures.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit (optional)
visa_steps.description: Through employment, business or buying property from $100,000 — a path to long-term status.

faq.question: Which language should I learn in Tbilisi?
faq.answer: Georgian for simple situations, but most people in Tbilisi understand Russian and English.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian ruble card in Tbilisi?
faq.answer: No, you need lari or foreign currency to exchange. The MIR card doesn't work.

faq.question: Where can I open a bank account in Tbilisi?
faq.answer: Bank of Georgia and TBC Bank — both work with Russians and issue cards with international payments.

faq.question: What is healthcare like in Tbilisi?
faq.answer: A private clinic appointment costs from 3,000 ₽. Quality is higher than at public facilities.

faq.question: How is the internet in Tbilisi?
faq.answer: Stable fibre in most districts, plans run 1,000–2,500 ₽ for 100+ Mbps.

faq.question: Is Tbilisi safe?
faq.answer: One of the safest cities in the region — low crime and friendly people.

reviews.text: Tbilisi is the best trade-off between cost and quality of life. In six months I opened a bank account, found an apartment and built a social circle.
The cultural difference scared me, but Tbilisi turned out to be an open city. Prices are rising, but it's still 2–3 times cheaper than Moscow.
